cues.say: Component 1: CDN. Servers around the world that keep copies of your site's files (pages, images, scripts) and serve each visitor from one nearby. You'll bring this up during version one, when you draw the basic design.
Think of it as: Local warehouses stocking your product, so not every order ships from the factory. Use it for every design, first spike defense, and files that rarely change.
Here's a real scenario. A bike shop's site gets shared on a forum: 50,000 visitors in an hour, about 2 megabytes each.
Without it: Every page, photo and script comes from the shop's 2 servers.
They max out, and pages crawl.
With it: First visitor per region: 1 fetch from the shop.
Everyone after: served by a nearby CDN server.
Shop servers only see cart and checkout.
Why it works: The files are the same for everyone, so don't make your servers send them every time.
In the interview, say: The CDN takes most of the read spike before it reaches us.
A few related terms you may hear.
DNS: The internet's phone book: pizza.com to a server address.
Low DNS TTL: Set it before launch, so you can redirect traffic fast.
